draft.title: Electron shells and the Bohr model
card: In the Bohr model, electrons orbit the nucleus in layers called shells. Each shell can hold only a set number of electrons.
The first shell holds up to 2 electrons. The second holds up to 8, and so does the third.
Electrons fill the shell closest to the nucleus first. Only when it is full do they start the next shell.
The outer shell is the outermost shell that holds electrons. The number of electrons in it decides how an element reacts.
draft.remember: Shells fill from the inside out, and the outer shell sets how an element reacts.

a.q: Which shows how the 11 electrons of a sodium atom are arranged in shells?
a.why: The first shell fills with 2, the second fills with 8, and the last 1 electron goes in the third shell. 2, 9 is wrong because the second shell holds only 8.
a.clue: Fill the shell closest to the nucleus first.

b.q: Priya says a chlorine atom has 17 electrons, so its outer shell holds 17. What is her mistake, and what is the correct outer shell?
opts: Shells hold set numbers, so the outer shell has 7
Shells hold set numbers, so the outer shell has 8
Only the first shell holds electrons, so it has 2
The outer shell holds all electrons, so it has 15
b.why: Electrons are spread over shells as 2, 8, 7, so the outer shell holds 7. It is not 8, because the third shell is not full. Priya forgot that inner shells fill first and hold set numbers.
b.clue: Fill 2, then 8, then see how many are left over.

b.best: Shells hold set numbers, so the outer shell has 7

problems.detail: The distractor 'The outer shell holds all electrons, so it has 15' contradicts itself. If the outer shell held all electrons it would have 17, not 15, which could confuse students. Make the reasoning match the number, or replace the option.

check.summary: Both answers check out (sodium 2, 8, 1; chlorine outer shell 7), and the card matches the chapter. One question b distractor is self-contradictory ('holds all electrons, so it has 15') and should be reworded.
